{{Quote|You know, a gentleman would turn his back while a lady changes.''"<br />"''That's not the sort of changing most people have in mind. And you're no lady.''"<br />"''Sometimes I am.|[[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] and [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Zam Wesell">''[[Star Wars: Zam Wesell]]''</ref>}}
'''Clawdites''' were a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Zolan/Legends|Zolan]]. They were one of the few [[Changeling/Legends|shape-shifting]] species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and were sometimes referred to as '''Changelings'''.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|I'm a Clawdite, Jango. It's what we do.|Zam Wesell, on her shapeshifting abilities|<ref name="Star Wars: Zam Wesell" />}}
In their natural form, Clawdites had the appearance of [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] humanoids, and in fact had evolved from [[Reptomammal/Legends|reptomammals]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> They had sunken cheeks with a narrow nose and a small mouth. A thin line ran down their foreheads and creased the center of their noses. They possessed large [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] with slit-like pupils, and their irises could be yellow, gold, or blue.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> Their skin was considered to be rough, and ranged in color from green to yellow. Overall, their appearance was identical to that of their genetic forebears, the [[Zolander]]s.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref>

[[File:Clawdite2.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Clawdite taking on a new form while running from a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].]]
Due to genetic manipulation, Clawdites possessed the extremely rare ability to change their appearance. When using this ability, they could change the color and texture of their skin and eyes, mimicking the appearance of other similarly shaped beings, such as [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. Shifting into a [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]], a species with similar facial features, was considered easy.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Though they could not add physical mass to their bodies, they were able to form hair, and could make it quite long.<ref name="SWJF">[[Star Wars: Jango Fett (one-shot)|''Star Wars: Jango Fett'']]</ref> Clawdites were also able to mimic the appearance of clothing or jewelry, provided that the item laid directly on their skin, as it was merely a manipulation of their skin's texture.<ref name="UAA" /> They could not change the appearance of their actual clothing, and had to rely on [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] technology in order to change such items.<ref name="HH">''[[The Clone Wars: The Holocron Heist]]''</ref>

The growth of their abilities mainly relied upon a Clawdite's age. [[Youngling/Legends|Younglings]] were only able to change color, a talent that began at infancy, and baby Clawdites used different hues and colors to indicate their needs to their parents.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

Unlike most shape-changing species, the Clawdites' shifting abilities caused them great physical discomfort.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> While the range of their abilities varied in individuals, with both age and practice, they could work through the pain of changing in order to alter their appearance in more and more extreme ways.<ref name="SAV" /> Even the most talented Clawdite, however, lacked the fine coordination it would take to mimic a specific individual's appearance precisely.<ref name="UAA" /> Only a very talented Clawdite was able to [[Sleep/Legends|sleep]] and retain their altered form. If a Clawdite was suitably distracted or hurt, and certainly if they were killed, they would revert to their true form.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

[[File:Clawdite.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Clawdites shifted back to their natural appearance when dying.]]
It was thought to be impossible for a Clawdite to change their body structure or body mass,<ref name="UAA" /> though it appeared that some individual Clawdites, such as [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]], [[Rolsat Noviee]] and [[Nuri]], managed this feat through unknown means.<ref name="BFMD">''[[Boba Fett: Maze of Deception]]''</ref> As most sentient beings' bodies were composed mostly of [[Water/Legends|water]], [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologists]] speculated that the Clawdites' ability to change may have laid in the manipulation of water, and that Wesell may have been able to exert greater control over her body's water than most. It was further presumed by those in the field that Wesell used some sort of medical device or injected substance, or that she figured out how to expel and consume water in various quantities to reduce or increase her mass. Though scientists attempted to test their theories about Wesell, no Clawdites were willing to subject themselves to study, fearing repercussions or prejudice should their abilities be fully revealed.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|You're a Clawdite, too.''"<br />"''That doesn't make us sisters.|Zam Wesell, as she reveals her true identity to [[Holowan's decoy|another Clawdite]]|<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 5: The Shape-Shifter Strikes">''[[Star Wars Adventures 5: The Shape-Shifter Strikes]]''</ref>}}
By nature, Clawdites were quiet<ref name="UAA" /> and solitary beings, often shunning the company of others unless it benefited them.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> They viewed the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] pragmatically,<ref name="UAA" /> and were often harsh realists who were mistrustful and suspicious of others.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

[[File:CatoParasitti-DB.png|thumb|left|225px|Bounty hunter Cato Parasitti]]
Not all Clawdites used their shape-shifting abilities, but those who did undertook great physical pain and effort in order to do so. They often learned [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] and concentration techniques, over long periods of time, in order to maximize their capabilities. Clawdites had to treat their skin with specialized oils in order to prevent cracking or tearing of their skin, due to the difficulty in physically maintaining their disguises.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

While in their natural form, they were considered indistinguishable from their Zolander brethren, but the two could be distinguished via genetic examination.<ref name="UAA" />

The [[Mabari/Legends|Mabari]] were an ancient order of warriors from Zolan, which survived at least until the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Though a few Clawdites, like Zam Wesell, were allowed entry, it was predominantly composed of Zolanders. The Zolanders wisely presumed that training too many Clawdites in the ways of war could create a powerful group of shape-shifting fighters, capable of overthrowing their rule. Any Clawdites who were accepted were closely monitored, and were they to leave the order, they were forcibly pressured to leave their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] as well.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Those who joined the order often wore [[Mabari armor]]weave, and the group presented clasps to their adherents, which signified their ranks.<ref name="AoTCTVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

On their homeworld of Zolan, Clawdites were feared and shunned by the Zolanders, who were a deeply religious people. Among their many strong convictions, the Zolanders believed the Clawdites to be impure and sinful. Because of their prejudice, the Zolanders forced the Clawdites to live in slums all across the planet. These ghettos were secured, so that the Zolanders could prevent the Clawdites from spreading. This subjugation continued for centuries, and it wasn't until after [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] that they were able to change their situation. After the rise of their new government, the Clawdites held classes for schoolchildren, in order to teach them greater control and efficiency with their abilities.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

The few Clawdites who left their world most often took advantage of their natural abilities to join militaristic professions, such as [[Spy/Legends|spying]], [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]], and bounty hunting. Joining groups such as these were the rare occasions where Clawdites afforded their loyalty to others, and they saw it as a positive contribution to the galaxy. They often sought to protect the liberties of other species, sensing in their pain the disparity their own people suffered.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==History==
Hundreds of generations in the past, the planet of Zolan became bombarded with harmful solar [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]]. Zolander [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] experimented on a group of volunteers, activating dormant skin-changing genes in the volunteers' genetic codes. To the repulsion of the rest of the Zolanders, these volunteers gained the ability to change their appearance. As they passed their genes down, a new species was formed, and the Zolanders quickly sought to marginalize and restrict this new species. After suffering persecution at the hands of their brethren, the very beings who had made them what they were, the altered Zolanders decided to create a new name for their species, to distinguish themselves from those who oppressed them. They now called themselves Clawdites.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

[[File:ZamClawdite-SWCTP.png|thumb|right|200px|Noted Clawdite assassin Zam Wesell]]
Hundreds of years after the divergence of their species, the Clawdites still lived in subjugation on their homeworld.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] and the proceeding [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Clawdites formed a political government for the first time, and sought the help of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] (CIS).<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], leader of the Separatist movement, offered them freedom from the Zolanders, leading many to enlist in the war effort against the Republic.<ref name="SAV" /> Three Clawdites notably worked for the Separatists. The [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] Zam Wesell, an ally of [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango]] and [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], was hired to help Fett kill [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]].<ref name="AOTC" /> Another, [[Cato Parasitti/Legends|Cato Parasitti]], helped fellow hunter [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] in his mission to steal a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] from vaults of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]].<ref name="HH" /> [[Braxus Lyn]] also worked for the CIS as a [[Spy/Legends|spy]].<ref name="GAW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> Still, some Clawdites served the Republic during the conflict, like [[Bargu]] who was a Clawdite [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], and a contemporary of [[Tallisibeth Enwandung-Esterhazy]].<ref name="YDR">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref> The Clawdite's hopes of help from Dooku were shattered when Skywalker killed Dooku near the end of the Clone Wars.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

After the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] [[Blockade of Zolan|blockaded]] Zolan because [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] was afraid of changelings aiding the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="Sambra">{{GamerCite|10|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Clawdites}}</ref> The Clawdites were trapped on their planet and remained in subjugation while the Empire was in power. Following the death of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and the fracturing of his Empire, however, the Clawdites rose up once more and fought against the Zolanders, in what become the [[Zolan Civil War]]. Inspired by the actions of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Clawdites triumphed during the war, and gained control over seventy-five percent of their planet.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

Shortly after emerging victorious from their civil war, the Clawdites contacted the New Republic, and sought to become members of the new galactic government. Almost immediately, however, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invaded the galaxy, ignited a devastating [[Yuuzhan Vong War|war]]. A group of Clawdites formed [[Guile Company]], which served as an intelligence unit behind Yuuzhan Vong lines. With their members numbering just over one hundred, and entering the most hostile of enemy territories, the Clawdites suffered an extremely high casualty rate. Even still, Guile Company kept receiving new volunteers, and they selected only the best shape-shifters. Because the casualty rate was so high and their numbers galaxy-wide were so low, Clawdites who had children were disallowed into their ranks. Despite this, some hid the fact they had children from the recruiters, and managed to join.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

Guile Company remained intact after the war ended, and soon began work for the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

==Behind the scenes==
"[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Clawdites]]", which was published in ''[[Star Wars Gamer 10]]'', established that the Clawdite species was a product of artificial mutation from the Zolanders "a hundred generations" before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="Sambra" /> However, ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'' stated that the Clawdites evolved naturally on a homeworld with a long-running civil war between related humanoid subspecies. The Clawdites would develop the adaptation to shapeshift into the forms of these other subspecies in order to live among them without being killed.<ref name="AoTCTVD" /> Subsequent sources such as ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' stick with what established in "The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Clawdites."<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />
